papers.title: Neurocognitive sequelae following seronegative anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis with ovarian teratoma in a pediatric patient: A six-year follow-up case report.
papers.reason: Long-term neuropsychological testing documents executive-function, attention, processing-speed, and memory deficits after pediatric encephalitis, although the evidence is limited to one case.

papers.title: Early Catheter Ablation for Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and a Stroke History: A Target Trial Emulation Analysis.
papers.reason: The study concerns catheter-ablation outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation and does not indicate any analysis of cognition or executive function.

papers.title: Beyond neurocentrism: situating cognition within the metabolic demands of the whole organism.
papers.reason: Its organism-level metabolic account of cognition may provide broad biological context, but the title does not indicate specific findings or models of executive function.

papers.title: REM sleep EEG slowing signals basal forebrain integrity in older adults with subjective and mild cognitive impairment
papers.reason: The paper evaluates a sleep-EEG signal as a neural biomarker in subjective and mild cognitive impairment, directly supporting early cognitive-impairment assessment despite not targeting executive function specifically.

papers.title: Consensus-Defined Sarcopenic Obesity and a Related Dynapenic Obesity Phenotype in Relation to Early Cognitive Impairment.
papers.reason: The study relates physical phenotypes to early cognitive impairment but does not appear to model executive processes or develop a behavioural, eye-tracking, or EEG biomarker.

papers.title: Circulating phosphatidylserine as a plasma biomarker for clinical staging and prognostic prediction in Parkinson's disease: A diagnostic validation study.
papers.reason: This is a plasma biomarker study for Parkinson's disease staging and prognosis with no stated connection to executive-function modelling or digital cognitive assessment.

papers.title: EndoPRS-SS: Summary-statistic based incorporation of endophenotypes to improve risk prediction.
papers.reason: The genetic risk-prediction method uses executive-function scores as an endophenotype that improves Alzheimer's disease prediction, but executive cognition is not itself modelled.

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnea severity associates with reduced phase-lag index functional connectivity during N2 sleep
papers.reason: The reported sleep connectivity association concerns obstructive sleep apnea without a stated cognitive, executive-function, or cognitive-classification outcome.

papers.title: Blunted Neural Error Monitoring Amplifies the Adverse Effect of Childhood Maltreatment on Depressive Symptoms: Time-Domain and Time-Frequency Analysis.
papers.reason: Time-domain and time-frequency measures of neural error monitoring provide directly relevant evidence about a core cognitive-control process, though the primary application is depression following maltreatment.

papers.title: Optimizing frailty care: an analysis of dual exercise targets and cognitive function among frail older adults.
papers.reason: The study associates fitness and strength with brief MoCA-defined cognitive impairment but does not isolate executive function or develop a process model or digital biomarker.

papers.title: Electroencephalography in Subjective Cognitive Decline and Mild Cognitive Impairment: Systematic Review of Biomarkers, Classification, and Prognostic Evidence
papers.reason: This systematic review directly synthesizes EEG biomarkers, classification models, and prognostic evidence for subjective cognitive decline and MCI, closely matching early-detection methodology despite very low evidence certainty.

papers.title: Association of Sarcopenia With Global, Motor, Cognitive, and Swallowing Function Prognosis in Stroke Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
papers.reason: The meta-analysis includes global cognitive prognosis after stroke as one of several outcomes but provides no executive-function-specific modelling or cognitive biomarker methodology.

papers.title: Oxygen extraction fraction mapping between normal cognition and mild cognitive impairment in older adults using quantitative BOLD
papers.reason: The paper applies Bayesian quantitative BOLD modelling to identify physiological differences in MCI, but its cognitive analysis emphasizes episodic memory rather than executive function.

papers.title: Factor Structure of the Neuropsychological Battery in the Mexican Cognitive Aging Ancillary Study (Mex-Cog)
papers.reason: Confirmatory factor analysis validates executive functioning as one of five domains in a large aging-assessment battery, providing useful psychometric structure for cognitive assessment without modelling executive processes.
